about: andrey.dagma at its defaults against the authors' dagma package on linear SEMs at the papers' densities, with the empty graph as the floor: one row per cell of the 24 standardized decision cells and of the 18 raw and 18 rescaled cells, 20 datasets each, seeds 0 to 19, and the rerun on seeds 20 to 39 of the one rescaled cell that came out worse than the reference. The reference and the empty graph are the recorded rows of the same datasets
build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 (the 0.17.0 release branch), the default fit of the 0.17.0 release

references.dagma: the authors' package dagma 1.1.1, DagmaLinear(loss_type='l2').fit(X, lambda1=0.03), w_threshold 0.3

verdict_rule: Decision cells: the standardized ones, 24 (ER2 and SF4; 10, 20, 50, 100 variables; Gaussian, exponential, Gumbel noise; 20 datasets each, seeds 0-19). Per cell D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D over 10,000 resamples lies wholly above 0, better when wholly below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs are not judged. Floor: the same interval of SHD(Andrey) - SHD(empty graph), which applies only where the reference's interval against the empty graph lies wholly below 0. The raw and rescaled cells are reported and do not decide

likelihood_path.about: robust=True of andrey.dagma and andrey.notears, the likelihood path of Deng et al. (2024) after the least-squares fit, before and after the term -log|det(I - W)| left its likelihood, beside the same path run with the authors' code and the empty graph, on the same datasets. One row per method, graph, size and scale; every value is a mean over the row's datasets
likelihood_path.data: the simulation of Deng et al. (2024), Appendix D.1, drawn with the simulator of the authors' package dagrad: linear Gaussian models, weights uniform on +-[0.5, 1.5], one noise standard deviation per variable uniform on [0.1, 0.7], 1,000 rows, Erdos-Renyi (er2) and scale-free (sf2) graphs with 2 d edges, columns shuffled; standardized z-scores each column of the drawn sample
likelihood_path.metric: SHD between the CPDAG of the estimate and the CPDAG of the true DAG, the measure of Deng et al. (2024)

arms.before: Andrey pre-release build of 14 November 2026, whose robust=True likelihood includes the term -log|det(I - W)|; the method at its defaults with robust=True
arms.now: Andrey pre-release build of 15 November 2026, whose continuous fits are those of the 0.18.0 release: the likelihood of robust=True without the term -log|det(I - W)|; the method at its defaults with robust=True
arms.reference: Algorithm 1 of Deng et al. (2024) as printed, around the unmodified single fits of the authors' package dagrad (commit 4ce4c5a): the warm start is dagrad's least-squares fit at its defaults, each step solves loss_fn='logll' with reg='mcp' from the last accepted weights at lambda 0.4 and delta 0.2, both times 0.8 after each accepted step, a step is accepted while the Gaussian negative log-likelihood strictly falls, and each fit is thresholded at 0.3, dagrad's default. For dagma rows the solver is method='dagma'; for notears rows method='notears' with optimizer='adam'. The paper gives no cap on the steps; the run allowed 50, which no fit reached. A cyclic output is repaired outside the authors' code by dropping the weakest edges until no cycle is left (reference_outputs_repaired counts the datasets)

likelihood_path.comparison: per dataset D = SHD(a) - SHD(b); bootstrap_95 is the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D over 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0); better when it lies wholly below 0, worse when wholly above, a tie otherwise
likelihood_path.protocol: each fit in its own process with one BLAS thread, on nodes of AMD EPYC processors of the Zen 3 generation; a cap per fit of 2,400 s (the fits of the build after, and NOTEARS's of the build before) or 1,800 s (DAGMA's of the build before, and the reference's), which no fit reached; times are not published

sachs.about: andrey.dagma and andrey.notears, at their defaults and with robust=True, beside andrey.pc and andrey.ges at their defaults, on the Sachs data, raw and with every column z-scored. One row per method, sample and scale: all_rows is the error of the fit on every row, and resample_mean the mean error over 10 resamples of the rows
sachs.data: andrey.load_dataset('sachs'): 11 proteins and phospholipids; 853 observational measurements (conditions=False) and the 7,466 measurements of all nine experimental conditions (conditions=True), read as one sample
sachs.truth: the consensus network of the dataset, 17 edges
sachs.metric: SHD between the CPDAG of the estimate and the CPDAG of the consensus network; pc and ges return a CPDAG, which is compared as returned
sachs.resampling: rows drawn with replacement to the sample's size, default_rng(b) for b = 0 to 9; a standardized fit z-scores the resampled rows

varsortability.what: varsortability of the consensus network on the 853 observational measurements (Reisach et al., 2021)

sachs.build: Andrey pre-release build of 15 November 2026, whose continuous fits are those of the 0.18.0 release: the likelihood of robust=True without the term -log|det(I - W)|
sachs.protocol: each fit in its own process with one BLAS thread, on a node of AMD EPYC processors of the Zen 3 generation; a cap of 900 s per fit, which no fit reached; no fit failed; times are not published
